extracted.intended_audience: users of the L-function numerical package / computational number theorists / PARI/GP users
extracted.subtask_description: Using and preparing data for the L-function / theta-function routines (lfun*, lfuntheta*, etc.) in the described numerical library; includes input formats, initialization, precision/performance tradeoffs, and diagnostic checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision in bits (use realbitprecision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requested precision for L-function routines is specified in bits; realbitprecision controls the returned absolute error B used throughout (results reported with absolute error < 2^{-B}). realprecision increases in coarse 64-bit increments and thus is less fine-grained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manipulate precision via realbitprecision for finer granularity. Increasing requested precision has a major impact on runtimes. If θ(t) is very small, increase realbitprecision by −log2|θ(t)| to get meaningful functional-equation checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation caveat: not for proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: The implementation assumes implied constants in O(...) are small and is intended for experimentation rather than producing rigorous proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat numerical results with caution; increase realbitprecision and recompute to estimate absolute error. The package cannot return proven results without more detailed L-function information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-dual L-function detection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the coefficient sequence a is real and a = a*, the L-function is said to be self-dual (this forces |ε| = 1 in many cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain optimizations or assumptions (e.g., real-valuedness of Hardy Z-function) apply to self-dual L-functions; user may use sentinel values when creating Ldata (see lfuncreate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide exact Ldata components when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: An Ldata should contain the complete datum [a, a*, A, k, N, eps, r]; all components should be given exactly because required accuracy is unbounded a priori.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice some components (local factors A, polar part r) may be unknown; the package offers routines to try to compute missing invariants but user-supplied exact data is preferred to ensure correct/routine behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-level data model (Lmath, Ldata, Linit)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three levels of description: Lmath (mathematical description), Ldata (computational description), Linit (initialized data for fast evaluation over a domain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For single evaluations you may pass Lmath or Ldata directly to lfun; for many evaluations (plots, zero searches) construct an Linit for the search range with lfuninit to avoid repeated initialization. Using an Linit outside its initialized domain triggers a warning and causes reinitialization (inefficient).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain initialization matters (lfuninit sdom)
rubrics_metrics.description: lfuninit(L, sdom, der) initializes computations on a rectangular/strip domain sdom = [center, w, h] (or shorthand forms). The height h of the domain is crucial: if only real s are needed set h = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the smallest rectangular domain you need. Cost scales strongly with the domain parameters; initializing up to maximal t needed is critical to avoid repeated warnings and slowdowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost/complexity estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of coefficients required scales as roughly O(N^{1/2}(|t|+1)^{1/2}) (the implementation requires O(N^{1/2}(|t|+1)^{1/2}) coefficients an to evaluate at s = σ + it). Running time is roughly proportional to (B/d + πh/4)^{d/2+3} N^{1/2} (exponent reduced for low degree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lfuncost / lfunthetacost to estimate costs. Expect cost to explode with large conductor N, high height h, or much higher bit precision B. Factorization (e.g., abelian fields) may reduce actual cost; lfuncost may return a vector of component costs in factorized cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of lfuncost / lfunthetacost
rubrics_metrics.description: lfuncost(L, sdom, der) and lfunthetacost(L, tdom, m) estimate the number of coefficients an and bit accuracy that will be computed for a planned initialization/evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call these before expensive inits to anticipate memory/time. When L is already an Linit, sdom/tdom are ignored and the function estimates cost for that Linit. Costs can be dramatically reduced when algebraic factorization is discovered upon initialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input format: Dirichlet character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Only primitive Dirichlet characters are supported. Several encodings are accepted (Conrey notation t_INTMOD, znstar structures, Conrey logarithms). Non-primitive characters are replaced by the attached primitive character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conrey-log format is the fastest; direct znstar or Conrey index formats are supported. Quadratic Kronecker symbols are encoded by t_INT with fundamental discriminant D (D = 1 gives Riemann zeta).

rubrics_metrics.name: Input format: Hecke characters / ray class
rubrics_metrics.description: Hecke characters are encoded via bnr structures (bnrinit), where the ray class group decomposition K.cyc and K.gen give di and gi, and characters are row vectors v describing values on generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For K = Q (Dirichlet characters) the bnr construction works but is less efficient than the direct Dirichlet construction. Pick the simpler direct constructor when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input format: Artin representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Artin L-functions are created with lfunartin given a Galois number field and a representation ρ specified either by character values on conjugacy classes or by matrices giving images of generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cyclotomic numbers in rho are given by polynomials whose variable stands for exp(2πi/n). Ensure polynomial variable priorities are set correctly (cyclotomic variable priority lower than x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elliptic/genus-2 curve L-functions: model requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Elliptic curve L-functions and genus-2 hyperelliptic curves are supported, but the model currently needs to be minimal at 2; if the conductor is even its 2-adic valuation might be incorrect (a warning is issued).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect warnings for even conductors; check and correct minimal models at small primes if accuracy of conductor is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eta-quotients / modular-form assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: lfunetaquo constructs Ldata for eta-quotients; it is currently assumed that f is a self-dual cuspidal form on Γ0(N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This routine accepts a matrix [m, r_m] rows giving η(mτ)^{r_m}; as a shorthand a single-row vector is accepted. More general modular-forms (modular symbols) planned for later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-level lfuncreate formats for a(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: V[1] (a) encodes Dirichlet series coefficients. Preferred format is a closure n -> vector(n, i, a(i)) returning the first n coefficients. Shortcut: pass a fixed vector v (closure n->v allowed). Alternative: closure (p,d)->F(p) giving local factor for Euler-product-capable L-functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closures may return more than n entries (only first n used) or less (loss of accuracy -> warning). For Euler-product closures the second argument d = floor(log_p n)+1 can be used to compute only needed local-factor precision; you may also supply bad local factors via dir = [F, Lbad]. When possible prefer high-level constructors over low-level lfuncreate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifying the dual coefficients astar
rubrics_metrics.description: V[2] = astar encodes the dual Dirichlet coefficients; special sentinel values 0 and 1 may be used for the common cases astar = a and astar = a*, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a != a*, you must input astar explicitly; otherwise use sentinel shortcut to simplify input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gamma-factor alphas Vga must be exact rationals
rubrics_metrics.description: V[3] = Vga is the vector of α_j in the gamma-factor γA(s) = ∏ Γ_R(s + α_j). In current implementation α_j are assumed to be exact rational numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using theta functions with complex arguments, non-integer α_j may cause determination problems and wrong results; prefer integral/rational α_j and be cautious with complex t.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight k and growth bound k1
rubrics_metrics.description: V[4] = k is a positive integer (functional equation relates s and k − s). By default an = O(n^{k1 + ε}) with k1 = w (w = k − 1), or k1 = w/2 when L has no pole (Ramanujan-Petersson). You may replace k with [k, k1] to supply a different growth bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tighter k1 if an grows faster than default to avoid incorrect assumptions; for motivic L-functions note w = k − 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conductor N must be integer ≥ 1
rubrics_metrics.description: V[5] = N is the conductor integer N ≥ 1 used in Λ(s) = N^{s/2} γ_A(s) L(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you know the local prime exponents of N, use them in constructing Ldata or use lfuncheckfeq to search efficiently rather than lfunconductor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Root number eps specification
rubrics_metrics.description: V[6] = eps is the root number ε such that Λ(a, k − s) = ε Λ(a*, s); usually |ε| = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure of ε, some routines (lfunrootres, lfuncheckfeq) can attempt to determine/estimate it given enough polar data or by consistency checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poles / polar part encoding requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: V[7] = poles encodes poles of L or Λ as a list of [β, P_β(x)] where P_β(x) is the polar part series. If L has poles, this must be provided; for Λ the type of list distinguishes L vs Λ poles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a != a* it is mandatory to specify the polar part of Λ rather than those of L since poles of L* cannot be inferred. If a = a* and L has at most a simple pole at s = k with residue r, you may specify poles = r (set r = 0 if unknown and it will be computed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check functional equation with lfuncheckfeq
rubrics_metrics.description: lfuncheckfeq(L,{t}) checks whether the functional equation is satisfied for provided data (Lmath/Ldata/Linit). It returns a bit accuracy b such that |w − ŵ| < 2^{-b}, where ŵ = θ(1/t) t^{-k} / θ(t) is computed from theta values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If t omitted, random samples in [1,1.25] are used. For efficiency choose t close to the unit disc and with θ(t) ≠ 0. If θ(t) is very small increase realbitprecision first. Checking away from the unit disc may fail with precision errors or give poor results.

rubrics_metrics.name: lfunconductor is heuristic (use cautiously)
rubrics_metrics.description: lfunconductor(L, ab, flag) attempts to compute the conductor heuristically over an interval ab; results are not proven and depend on precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lfunconductor only when primes dividing conductor are unknown. If local primes are known, prefer direct search via lfuncheckfeq for a more rigorous result. ab enlarges search interval but increases runtime; flag controls rounding behavior of returned conductors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer lfuninit before many evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: When many values will be computed, construct an Linit via lfuninit(L, sdom, der) and use it for subsequent lfun calls to avoid costly reinitializations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For single-evaluation use lfun(L,s) directly. Attempting derivatives beyond the Linit der parameter will cause warnings or reinitialization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output error bounds for lfun/lfunlambda/lfuntheta
rubrics_metrics.description: lfun(L,s,D) returns L(s) or derivatives with absolute error < 2^{-B}, where B = realbitprecision. lfunlambda returns Λ(s) with absolute error < 2^{-B} |γ(s) N^{s/2}|. lfuntheta returns theta derivatives with absolute error < 2^{-B}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret returned values accordingly; to reduce error increase realbitprecision. lfun accepts power-series s to return Taylor expansions, with order determined by O(x^n) input.

rubrics_metrics.name: lfunrootres behavior depends on polar knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: lfunrootres(data) returns polar parts and root number; if all polar parts are known the function determines the root number exactly; otherwise at most a single pole is allowed and the routine computes root number and residue (0 if none).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete polar part description when possible to allow full determination. The output format is [[[a1,r1],...], [[b1,R1],...], w].

rubrics_metrics.name: lfunorderzero default order heuristics and override
rubrics_metrics.description: lfunorderzero(L,{m=-1}) computes order of possible zero at center k/2. If m ≥ 0 is given it assumes order ≤ m. Otherwise default m is chosen: if L is an Linit assume order ≤ maximal derivation order; else assume order < 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may explicitly increase m to force a larger search (may force recomputation of Linit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta function definition and relation to functional equation
rubrics_metrics.description: θ(a,t) defined by inverse Mellin transform of Λ(s) (with choice of c), satisfies θ(a,1/t) − ε t^k θ(a*,t) = P_Λ(t) where P_Λ(t) is polynomial/polar contribution; θ is often easier to compute than L(s) and useful to guess missing invariants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: θ(t) is analytic for complex t in a cone containing positive real axis; there are no log terms if poles are simple and P_Λ = 0 if Λ is entire. Use theta functional equation to infer polar/residue data or to check consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: lfunthetainit t-domain constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: lfunthetainit(L, tdom, m) initializes theta evaluations for t in domain tdom. tdom may be omitted (defaults to real t≥1), a positive real scalar ρ (real t≥ρ), a complex t (compute at that t and for cone defined by |t| and arg(t)), or [ρ,α] (|t|≥ρ and |arg t| ≤ α).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The constraint |2 arg z/d| < π/2 must hold (d = degree of Γ factor). lfunthetainit(L, tdom) is equivalent to lfunthetainit(L, [abs(t), arg(t)]). lfunthetacost/lfunthetainit will signal domain errors if domain violates allowed cone.

rubrics_metrics.name: lfuntheta direct vs initialized usage
rubrics_metrics.description: You may compute θ(t) directly via lfuntheta(L,t) or initialize once with T = lfunthetainit(L, tdom) and then call lfuntheta(T, t) for instantaneous evaluations within the domain cone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For many theta evaluations initialize once; attempting to use initialized T outside its domain raises domain errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: lfunzeros: naive zero-finding and divz parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: lfunzeros(L, lim, {divz=8}) computes zeros on the critical line using a naive mesh which may miss zeros. It assumes consecutive zeros at height T ≥ 1 differ by at least 2π/ω where ω := divz · ( d log(T/2π) + d + 2 log(N/(π/2)^d ) ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To use a finer search mesh increase divz above the default 8. Be aware the algorithm is heuristic and can miss closely spaced zeros.

rubrics_metrics.name: lfuncost and cost reduction by factorization
rubrics_metrics.description: lfuncost may return an a priori cost vector; if the L-function factorizes algebraically when lfuninit is called, the actual cost (returned by lfuncost after initialization) may be much lower, possibly giving separate component costs for each factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you expect algebraic factorization (e.g., Dedekind zeta of abelian fields), call lfuninit and then lfuncost to obtain the realistic cost distribution. Use this to choose efficient evaluation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: lfundiv / lfunmul pole/zero constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: lflundiv(L1,L2) and lfunmul(L1,L2) create Ldata for quotient/product of Dirichlet series, assuming vz(L1) ≥ vz(L2) at all complex z: construction may not create new poles or increase the order of existing ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure inputs satisfy the no-new-poles condition; these functions only create Ldata (no initialization) and require bitprec argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behaviour with derivatives D parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: Many functions accept {D = 0} or {der} parameters indicating derivative order; initialization must account for maximum derivative order (der) that will be used, otherwise warnings/inefficiencies or re-initialization occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you intend to compute derivatives (e.g., lfun(L,s,D) or lfuntheta m-th derivative), include der/m in lfuninit/lfunthetainit to precompute the needed structures and avoid repeated initialization warnings.
